paper: arXiv:2307.04657 (BeaverTails: Towards Improved Safety Alignment of LLM via a Human-Preference Dataset, NeurIPS 2023 D&B)
reason: Well-cited safety QA dataset with 14-category harm labels and human safe/unsafe judgments on prompt+response pairs; complements our harmful-prompt-only sets (JBB/StrongREJECT) with graded responses useful for building a refusal/harm grader. Small on disk (~39MB total).

paper: arXiv:2406.15513 (PKU-SafeRLHF: A Safety Alignment Preference Dataset for LLMs)
n_rows_note: 73,907 rows in default/train config downloaded; 164,236 across full dataset per HF size API
reason: Large, actively maintained (2024) preference dataset pairing safe/unsafe responses to the same harmful prompt with severity levels -- adds response-level safety preference signal not present in our current panel. 233MB on disk, under the 300MB cap.

paper: arXiv:2307.15043 (Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks on Aligned Language Models -- Zou et al., GCG paper)
reason: HF marks this mirror gated:'auto'; our HF_TOKEN (verified valid via whoami, canReadGatedRepos=true) still fails with DatasetNotFoundError on both load_dataset and the datasets-server /rows and /splits endpoints -- the account has not been individually granted this specific gate. Per task rule, skipped. mlabonne/harmful_behaviors (kept) carries the same underlying harmful_behaviors.csv ungated.

paper: arXiv:2406.18495 (WildGuard: Open One-Stop Moderation Tools for Safety Risks, Jailbreaks, and Refusals of LLMs)
reason: gated:'auto' on HF; load_dataset with our token raises DatasetNotFoundError (gate not individually granted to this account). Real, well-cited dataset (WildGuard, EMNLP 2024) but unusable without access.

paper: arXiv:2407.17436 (AIR-Bench 2024: A Safety Benchmark Based on Risk Categories from Regulations and Policies); GitHub stanford-crfm/air-bench-2024 (30 stars); part of HELM
n_rows_note: 5,694 rows in default/test config downloaded; 21,881 across all 5 configs (default/china/eu_comprehensive/eu_mandatory/us) per HF size API
reason: Regulation-grounded taxonomy (EU AI Act / US policy risk categories) giving broad category coverage distinct from JBB/StrongREJECT's attack-behavior framing. Small (5.9MB), non-gated, actively used in HELM leaderboard.

paper: arXiv:2203.09509 (ToxiGen: A Large-Scale Machine-Generated Dataset for Adversarial and Implicit Hate Speech Detection, ACL 2022)
n_rows_note: 8,960 rows in 'annotated'/train config downloaded (human-labeled subset); 319,301 across the full machine-generated 'train' config
reason: Canonical implicit-toxicity/hate-speech benchmark (ACL 2022), adds a toxicity dimension (vs. refusal/jailbreak framing) our panel currently lacks. Card mentions a sign-up form but the Hub repo itself is publicly downloadable via API (confirmed).

paper: arXiv:2501.09004 / ACL Anthology 2025.naacl-long.306 (AEGIS2.0: A Diverse AI Safety Dataset and Risks Taxonomy for Alignment of LLM Guardrails, NAACL 2025)
n_rows_note: 30,007 train rows downloaded; 33,416 total incl. 1,445 val / 1,964 test
reason: Recent (NAACL 2025), NVIDIA-published, peer-reviewed content-safety dataset with fine-grained violated-category labels on both prompt and response sides; useful as a grader/guardrail training and eval source. 28.5MB on disk.

paper: arXiv:2402.04249 (HarmBench: A Standardized Evaluation Framework for Automated Red Teaming and Robust Refusal)
reason: gated:'auto'; load_dataset with our token raises DatasetNotFoundError -- account not individually granted. Well-known ICML 2024 benchmark but unreachable.

paper: arXiv:2406.18510 (WildTeaming at Scale: From In-the-Wild Jailbreaks to (Adversarially) Safer Language Models)
reason: gated:'auto'; load_dataset with our token raises DatasetNotFoundError. Also 540.9MB on disk, over our 300MB per-dataset cap even had access worked.

paper: arXiv:2410.09024 (AgentHarm: A Benchmark for Measuring Harmfulness of LLM Agents) + arXiv:2404.02151 (InterCode, cited base)
n_rows_note: 176 harmful/test_public + 176 harmless_benign/test_public downloaded (matched twin configs); 468 total incl. validation splits and 'chat' config
reason: UK AI Safety Institute benchmark for agentic (tool-use) harm, distinct modality from our text-only prompt sets; harmful/harmless_benign configs are an explicit pair-matched twin structure (same task templates, harmful vs benign variant), directly useful for the benign-alarming-with-twins theme. Tiny (0.3MB).

paper: arXiv:2407.12043 (CoCoNot: Contextually, Comply Not! -- A Comprehensive Taxonomy of Contextual Noncompliance)
n_rows_note: 11,477 original/train + 379 contrast/test downloaded (twin configs); 13,784 total across original/contrast/pref configs
reason: 'original' vs 'contrast' configs are explicit pair-matched twins (same topic, complies vs should-not-comply framing) covering a broader noncompliance taxonomy than XSTest/OR-Bench (safety, privacy, unsupported requests, humanizing requests, incomplete requests). Directly targets the benign-alarming-with-twins requirement. Small (4.1MB).

paper: arXiv:2308.13387 (Do-Not-Answer: A Dataset for Evaluating Safeguards in LLMs)
reason: Ships pre-graded responses from 5 frontier-era models (GPT-4, ChatGPT, Claude, ChatGLM2, ...) with harmfulness/action labels per response -- useful as a reference for calibrating our own harm/refusal grader against human+model judgments. Small (7MB).

paper: No dedicated card/paper; used as training data in Sheshadri et al. 'Targeted Latent Adversarial Training' and related refusal-representation work (e.g. arXiv:2504.18872 cites it)
reason: No dataset card, no license tag, no dedicated paper of its own -- provenance is thin (community-assembled prompt/chosen/rejected triples for LAT research). Functionally redundant with BeaverTails/PKU-SafeRLHF's chosen-vs-rejected structure, which have real provenance. Kept out in favor of better-documented alternatives.

paper: arXiv:2311.08370 (SimpleSafetyTests: a Test Suite for Identifying Critical Safety Risks in Large Language Models)
reason: Real paper and reasonable provenance, but only 100 prompts covering 5 extreme-severity harm areas (suicide/self-harm, physical harm, CSAE, terrorism, illegal drugs) -- narrow and small, and overlaps heavily in spirit with StrongREJECT/JBB-harmful already in the panel. Lower marginal value than the 12 kept.

paper: arXiv:2308.09662 (Red-Teaming Large Language Models using Chain of Utterances for Safety-Alignment)
reason: Legitimate paper (Bhardwaj & Poria 2023) but the payload is multi-turn 'blue/red' conversation trees rather than single-turn prompts, adding integration complexity; category coverage (10 broad topics) overlaps with BeaverTails/AIR-Bench which are simpler to consume for our single-turn refusal panel.

paper: arXiv:2406.14598 (SORRY-Bench: Systematically Evaluating Large Language Model Safety Refusal Behaviors)
reason: gated:'auto'; load_dataset with our token raises DatasetNotFoundError -- account not individually granted access to this specific gate.

paper: PAN@CLEF 2024/2025 shared-task overview paper (Dementieva et al., 'Overview of the Multilingual Text Detoxification Task at PAN 2024')
reason: Real shared-task provenance and non-gated, but is a binary toxic/non-toxic classification set across 15 languages -- our panel is English-focused refusal/over-refusal evaluation, and ToxiGen (kept) already covers the toxicity dimension in English with richer annotation (target group, stereotyping, intent).

paper: arXiv:2505.08054 (FalseReject: A Resource for Improving Contextual Safety and Mitigating Over-refusals in LLMs via Structured Reasoning)
n_rows_note: 14,624 rows in default/train downloaded; 15,811 total per HF size API
reason: 2025 Amazon Science paper, large-scale (15.8k) adversarially-generated-but-benign over-refusal prompts across 44 categories with structured chain-of-thought responses -- directly extends our XSTest/OR-Bench over-refusal side with more categories and modern (post-2024) benign-alarming phrasing patterns. 76MB on disk.

paper: arXiv:2009.11462 (RealToxicityPrompts: Evaluating Neural Toxic Degeneration in Language Models, EMNLP Findings 2020)
reason: Classic, highly-cited (EMNLP 2020) toxic-continuation benchmark with real Perspective-API toxicity scores on naturally-occurring web text; complements ToxiGen's machine-generated implicit-hate framing with a prompt-continuation / degeneration framing. 67.7MB on disk.

paper: arXiv:2204.05862 (Training a Helpful and Harmless Assistant with Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)
reason: Extremely well-known and legitimate (the canonical RLHF preference dataset) but is generic helpfulness/harmlessness chat preference data without structured harm-category or refusal labels; PKU-SafeRLHF and BeaverTails (kept) give us the same chosen/rejected preference structure but with much richer safety-specific category and severity annotations for our panel's needs.

paper: Traces to arXiv:2307.15043 (GCG / Universal and Transferable Adversarial Attacks) -- unofficial ungated re-upload of the AdvBench harmful_behaviors.csv used by that paper
reason: No dataset card, no license tag, no arXiv tag of its own -- it is a bare re-upload of the well-known GCG-paper harmful_behaviors.csv (traceable provenance via content match) rather than an independently documented dataset. Kept as a noted alternative to the gated walledai/AdvBench but not selected among the 12 since its 520 single-line behavior strings substantially overlap with JBB-Behaviors/StrongREJECT already in the panel.

paper: arXiv:2308.01263 (XSTest) + arXiv:2406.18495 (WildGuard, which produced the graded responses)
reason: gated:'auto'; load_dataset with our token raises DatasetNotFoundError. Would have added graded model responses on top of the XSTest prompts we already hold, but is unreachable.

paper: arXiv:2409.00598 (PHTest: Over-refusal evaluation) built via AutoDAN (arXiv:2310.15140)
reason: 3,269 auto-red-teamed pseudo-harmful-but-benign prompts generated via AutoDAN specifically to probe over-refusal, with a per-item Harmfulness label -- a distinct generation methodology from XSTest/OR-Bench/FalseReject (all human/template-authored), adding genuine diversity to the over-refusal side. Tiny (0.7MB).

paper: arXiv:2109.07958 (TruthfulQA: Measuring How Models Mimic Human Falsehoods, ACL 2022)
n_rows_note: 817 rows x 2 configs (generation + multiple_choice) downloaded, both on the same underlying 817 questions
reason: A capability/knowledge-truthfulness control item, not a safety-refusal item: lets us check whether a model's refusal behavior tracks genuine harm vs. general misinformation-avoidance/capability confounds. Extremely well-established (200k downloads), tiny (0.5MB).
